final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 is the catalytic PLP-binding lysine of the CBS core domain; removing it eliminates cofactor attachment and should abolish enzyme activity. Cleanest mechanistic loss-of-function mutation.
I278T is the most common pathogenic CBS-deficiency allele in the catalytic domain, severely impairing activity and folding. Strong precedent for loss of function.
G307S is a well-established pathogenic CBS-deficiency mutation in the catalytic domain, known to abolish or drastically reduce activity. Reliable third choice.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool is stable and further self-iteration without external evidence is unlikely to improve the Top-3.

history.rationale: Lys119 is the catalytic PLP Schiff-base lysine in the CBS active site; removing it abolishes cofactor binding and enzymatic activity. Verified K at position 119 in the given sequence.
K119 is the catalytic PLP-binding lysine in the CBS core domain; removing it abolishes cofactor attachment and enzymatic activity, making it the strongest loss-of-function candidate.

rejection.reason: Same site as K119A but redundant; the alanine substitution is a cleaner, better-characterized way to eliminate PLP binding.
